newsitem.title: USA: Burger King remains strong competitor in burger wars.
newsitem.headline: Burger King remains strong competitor in burger wars.

text.p: Big Macs are 55 cents, Whoppers cost less than a dollar and Wendy's has a new sandwich on pita bread.
Such are the weapons in the continuing battle for market share in the fast food industry, and Monday's multi-billion dollar merger of Burger King's British parent is unlikely to lead to a truce.
Grand Metropolitan Plc agreed Monday to buy Guinness Plc for $15.8 billion, creating a giant food and drink company with brand including Burger King, Pillsbury, Johnnie Walker and Haagen Dazs.
"I don't see this merger having a material impact on Burger King's domestic strategy going forward," Natwest Securities analyst Damon Brundage said. "They are well-positioned in the U.S. right now."

Burger King is competing head-to-head with McDonald's Corp. in a battle to capture U.S. market share. McDonald's last month began its Campaign 55 price promotion, while Burger King is offering its signature Whopper hamburger for 99 cents.
Earlier Monday, Grand Metropolitan said the global outlook for Burger King remained good.

"There is significant scope for increasing both average unit volumes and the number of outlets," said Grand Metropolitan. Grand Met and Britain's Guinness Plc plan to merge, forming a company called GMG Brands.

Meanwhile, Wendy's International Inc. on May 1 unveiled national advertising for its four new pita sandwiches. Industry executives said Wendy's strategy has been to focus on new products instead of price promotions.

Wendy's pita sandwiches, which were rolled out gradually in the first quarter, contributed to record sales at its company-owned U.S. stores for the period from April 28 to May 4, said Denny Lynch, vice president of communications.
"In the midst of heavy discounting in the industry, we have been producing record sales," Lynch said Monday.

In Campaign 55, McDonald's is offering breakfast sandwiches and its Big Mac hamburgers for 55 cents when customers also purchase a drink and hash browns or french fries. Campaign 55 will feature the Quarter Pounder hamburger with cheese starting in June, McDonald's said.
McDonald's franchisee sources said that since Campaign 55, sales at many units have been flat with a year ago as the price promotion cut the size of the average customer check.

"Average check has dropped a couple of cents. But penny profit is probably as good if not maybe slightly better," said George Kunz, a McDonald's franchisee with six units in the Las Vegas area and chairman of the McDonald's Operators National Advertising Fund.
Profits are holding up, Kunz said, because the number of transactions has increased. The goal for Campaign 55 going forward, he added, is to increase customer transactions further to build profits.

McDonald's officials declined to comment today on Campaign 55, except to reiterate that U.S. same-store sales for the first four months of 1997 have been strong, bolstered by the sold-out Beanie Babies toy promotion for its Happy Meals.

Burger King said its 99-cent Whopper promotion has been aimed at bringing core customers in more frequently and attracting new consumers. "We believe it accomplishes both those tasks," Burger King spokeswoman Kim Miller said.
The campaigns by the three biggest chains underscore the continued intense competition in the fast food industry.
"It continues to be a market-share game," said Sid Feltenstein, president of A&W Restaurants and a fast-food industry veteran.
The goal of all the players is to increase the frequency of customer visits, Feltenstein said, through "good value at a fair price."

Fast-food chains will continue to rely on promotions to build customer traffic with Burger King launching a tie-in later this month with "The Lost World," the movie sequel to "Jurassic Park." At the same time, it will feature toy giveaways from the "Land Before Time" video series with its Kids' Club children meals.
McDonald's, under a 10-year exclusive alliance with Walt Disney Co., has announced promotions with "George of the Jungle" and "Hercules" movies.
